title: The Co-Evolutionary Arms Race Between Salmonella and the NLRC4 Inflammasome: Immune Recognition and Evasion Strategies
content: Salmonella is a globally significant foodborne intracellular pathogen, and invasive salmonellosis poses a major global public health threat. The NLR family CARD domain-containing protein 4 (NLRC4) inflammasome, a pivotal cytosolic innate immune sensor, specifically recognizes Salmonella flagellin and type III secretion system (T3SS) components via the NAIP (NLR family apoptosis inhibitory protein) family. Upon activation, it triggers pyroptosis, pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and infected intestinal epithelial cell extrusion, serving as a central pathway for host defense against Salmonella colonization and systemic spread. In this review, we systematically summarize the structural composition, activation mechanisms, post-translational modifications, and regulatory protein network of the NLRC4 inflammasome. This review highlights the molecular mechanisms by which Salmonella evades NLRC4 surveillance through multiple strategies: transcriptional downregulation of immunogenic ligands, structural modification of T3SS components, secretion of effector proteins, and chemotaxis-virulence synergy. This review comprehensively presents the co-evolutionary arms race between Salmonella and the NLRC4 inflammasome, providing a theoretical basis for elucidating bacterial immune evasion mechanisms and developing novel anti-infective targets.
